100004.testo: 🔑 Key Information Activity ⭐️ Title Unfolding Activity 🔶 Type | 📆 Dates | 📍Location Training Course 7-15 October 2026 | Talsi, Latvia 🌍 Erasmus+ explained — the complete beginner's guide to Europe's largest youth programme. Millions of young people have taken part in Erasmus+ since its launch, but many still don't fully understand what the programme actually includes, who it's for, or how to get involved. This in-depth guide breaks down everything: the different types of mobility, funding opportunities, eligibility criteria, and what you can realistically expect from participating. If you've ever wondered whether Erasmus+ is right for you, this guide gives you all the answers in one place. 👉 https://youthworkshub.org/15096/ ❗️ What Is This Training About? UNFOLDING aims to explore curiosity, challenges and creativity through outdoor activities, embodiment and facilitation practice to build adaptability, self-awareness and to reconnect with a curious mind in both personal & professional contexts. 🏘️ How Erasmus+ youth projects create lasting change in local communities. The impact of Erasmus+ goes far beyond the individuals who participate. Local communities, host organisations, and even entire neighbourhoods are shaped by the projects that take place within them. This article explores the broader social impact of Erasmus+ youth exchanges — from building intercultural understanding to empowering grassroots organisations — and makes a compelling case for why these projects matter beyond the personal level. 👉 https://youthworkshub.org/3595/ ℹ️ Description About The Opportunity UNFOLDING is a 7-day training program organized by MO(ve)MENT, and it's built on 3 main pillars that will flow throughout the whole project: curiosity, challenges and creativity. We believe that a curious mind keeps the learning alive and this learning experience aims to support youth workers in reconnecting with the ability to question, to listen, and to explore situations beyond what is already known or expected. During this project we aim to approach challenges as learning opportunities and practice fields for learning adaptability. We believe that youth work happens in motion and with “Unfolding”, we aim to strengthen the youth workers understanding of creating meaningful learning experiences for youth and leading group processes, react to group dynamic shifts and their own role within them. Through fostering self-awareness, embracing unpredictability and meeting curiosity, this project aims to strengthen youth workers’ ability to stay present, grounded and responsive in uncertain situations. During the project, participants will engage in a dynamic programe which will include outdoor challenges, artistic practices, embodiment, movement, dance, facilitation laboratory/practice, and nature based mindfulness practices. The program aims to create an open space to explore your personal limits and beliefs using the resources available within ourselves and the group. Who can apply? - This training course is created for youth workers, educators, social workers, trainers, facilitators or people working with people, especially youth. We aim to have 27 participants (aged 18+) from 6 countries - Latvia, Italy, Greece, Spain, Netherlands, Romania. To fully participate in the programe all applicants must have a communicative level of English. You must be willing to fully commit to the program of the project by actively participating in all of the activities and processes before, during, and after the project. You can expect to have an intensive program of 6-8 hours every day. Coming to the project later or leaving earlier is not allowed. 13983.testo: 🇱🇹 Erasmus+ Training Course in Lithuania 🎓 Learning Out Loud 🌍 Youth Work and Learning Recognition, SALTO 🇱🇹 Are you a youth worker, youth leader, mentor, or coach who believes in the learning potential of youth work — and wants to better support young people in recognising, reflecting on, and expressing what they learn? Learning Out Loud is an Erasmus+ Training Course organised by SALTO Training and Cooperation Resource Centre and the Lithuanian National Agency, designed to develop youth workers' competences in facilitating and recognising learning in youth work settings. Based on the Youthpass concept, the course combines a residential activity in Lithuania with pre- and post-course online sessions and individual micro-activities — offering a full learning journey rather than a single event. Accommodation and food covered by the Lithuanian NA. Travel reimbursement available through your National Agency or SALTO. Deadline: 19 April 2026. 🇱🇹 Did You Know? Lithuania has one of the most active National Agencies for Erasmus+ Youth in Europe — regularly organising and co-hosting international training courses, seminars, and study visits for youth workers across the continent. The country's youth sector has grown rapidly since EU accession in 2004 and is now deeply integrated into European non-formal education networks. The Lithuanian landscape — with its forests, lakes, and Baltic coastal scenery — also makes it one of the most atmospheric locations in Europe for a residential training course. What Will You Do? 🗣️ Discuss and exchange practices on the learning potential of youth work — exploring how and what young people actually learn through youth activities 🔍 Explore what supporting learning means in the role of a youth worker — and how to intentionally build reflection and recognition into your practice 🛠️ Practice concrete tools that support young people's learning process in youth work activities — taking these tools back into your own work context 📝 Learn practical approaches to formulating and documenting learning outcomes — so that young people's learning becomes visible to themselves and to others 🎓 Deepen your understanding of the Youthpass concept as a process for supporting reflective learning in youth projects — not just a certificate, but a pedagogical tool 💻 Participate in pre-course and post-course online group meetings — extending the learning beyond the residential days and embedding it in your ongoing practice 💡 Did You Know? Youthpass is an official European Commission tool that allows participants in Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps projects to document and describe their learning outcomes and competence development. Originally introduced in 2007, it is now used by hundreds of thousands of young people and youth workers across Europe each year — and is increasingly recognised by employers, universities, and institutions as evidence of non-formal learning. This training course is specifically designed to help youth workers use Youthpass not just as a document, but as a genuine learning facilitation process. Programme Structure 💻 Pre-course online group meeting: 13 May 2026, 10:00–11:30 CET — introduction and preparation before the residential phase 📋 Individual preparatory activities before the residential course — personalised tasks to help you arrive ready to engage deeply 🏡 Residential activity: 3–5 June 2026 in Lithuania — the core learning experience, fully facilitated and residential 🔄 Individual micro follow-up activities after the residential course — applying what you've learned back in your own youth work practice 💻 Post-course online group meeting: 23 June 2026, 10:00–11:30 CET — reflection, sharing, and consolidation of learning across the full group Who Can Apply? 🤝 You are a youth worker, youth leader, mentor, coach, or other practitioner who works regularly with young people — individually or in group settings, locally or internationally 💡 You believe in the learning potential of youth work and want to strengthen the quality of your practice around learning facilitation and recognition 🌍 You are interested in supporting young people in recognising, reflecting on, and expressing the value of their learning experiences 🗣️ You are at least 18 years old and able to actively communicate and work in English throughout the course ✅ You are able and willing to engage in all phases of the project — pre-course, residential, and post-course — full participation is expected and required ♿ The activity and venue are fully accessible to people with disabilities Costs & Practical Information 💰 Participation fee varies by country — financed by participating National Agencies. Contact your own National Agency or SALTO Resource Centre to find out the fee applicable for participants from your country 🏠 Accommodation and food during the event covered by the Lithuanian National Agency — no additional costs for board and lodging during the residential phase ✈️ Travel reimbursement may be available — contact your National Agency or SALTO to find out whether they support your travel costs and to learn the booking procedure 🎓 Youthpass certificate issued upon completion — official recognition of competence development during the activity Key Information 📅 Residential dates: 3 – 5 June 2026 📍 Location: Lithuania ⏳ Deadline: 19 April 2026 📣 Selection date: 4 May 2026 👥 Participants: 24 🗣️ Language: English Eligible Countries 🇦🇹 Austria, 🇧🇪 Belgium, 🇧🇬 Bulgaria, 🇭🇷 Croatia, 🇨🇾 Cyprus, 🇨🇿 Czech Republic, 🇩🇰 Denmark, 🇪🇪 Estonia, 🇫🇮 Finland, 🇫🇷 France, 🇩🇪 Germany, 🇬🇷 Greece, 🇭🇺 Hungary, 🇮🇸 Iceland, 🇮🇪 Ireland, 🇮🇹 Italy, 🇱🇻 Latvia, 🇱🇮 Liechtenstein, 🇱🇹 Lithuania, 🇱🇺 Luxembourg, 🇲🇹 Malta, 🇳🇱 Netherlands, 🇳🇴 Norway, 🇵🇱 Poland, 🇵🇹 Portugal, 🇲🇰 North Macedonia, 🇷🇴 Romania, 🇷🇸 Serbia, 🇸🇰 Slovakia, 🇸🇮 Slovenia, 🇪🇸 Spain, 🇸🇪 Sweden, 🇨🇭 Switzerland, 🇹🇷 Türkiye Application Link 🔗 Apply here: salto-youth.net — Learning Out Loud, Lithuania 📧 Contact: bakir@jfemail.de ⚠️ Important Notice 1️⃣ S

18571.testo: Self-care for non-formal educators Training Course 23-28 August 2026 | Estonia & Slovenia, Estonia You support others every day. But where do you reset? This programme supports educators to stay well in demanding roles and to shape healthier team environments. In Estonia, you focus on yourself. In Slovenia, you bring that awareness into your team. You support others every day. But where do you reset? This programme supports youth workers, facilitators, and educators to stay well in demanding roles and to shape healthier team environments. In Estonia, you focus on yourself. You explore your rhythms, boundaries, roles, and capacity. You learn how to notice what is yours and what is not, and how to take care of yourself in practice. In Slovenia, you bring that awareness into your team. You work with team dynamics, roles, and responsibility. You explore how to create safer, more sustainable ways of working together. Together, the two trainings move from personal awareness to team and system change. The programme combines: somatic (body-based) awareness reflective practices experiential learning with real cases systemic and team-based approaches TRAINING DATES Training 1 (Estonia) 23–28 August 2026 Self-care, resilience, and personal sustainability Training 2 (Slovenia) 25–30 October 2026 Team dynamics, safe space, and organisational wellbeing WHO IS THIS FOR? We are looking for participants who: work as youth workers, facilitators, trainers, or educators work with young people or in teams feel the impact of their work and want to stay well while doing it want to strengthen both personal resilience and team leadership LANGUAGE The whole programme will be held in English. You do not need perfect English, but you should feel comfortable enough to take part in group discussions, share your thoughts, and work in small groups. PARTICIPATION & GROUP The programme is designed as one learning journey. It is possible to join only one of the trainings. However, if selection is needed, priority will be given to participants who commit to both trainings. Group size: 20–25 participants WHAT WE EXPECT FROM PARTICIPANTS willingness to reflect on your own practice openness to share and listen readiness to engage in experiential methods commitment to the full programme If selected, participants are expected to: organise their own travel send travel tickets by the agreed deadline (end of June) respect communication and organisational timelines Registration is binding. Cancellation is only possible with a doctor’s certificate. OVERALL OBJECTIVE To support youth workers and facilitators to stay well in their roles and to create healthier, more sustainable team environments. HOW WE WORK We keep the process grounded and practical. You will work with real situations from your own context. You will not only talk about self-care but you will practice it. The trainings are built on: 1. Safety in practice co-created agreements clear boundaries facilitator transparency 2. A balanced learning process body awareness (what do you feel and notice?) frameworks (what helps you understand it?) experience (what happens in real situations?) reflection (what do you take from it?) 3. Objectives Networking between organisations that implement KA2 projects Disseminating and showcasing best KA2 project outcomes Highlighting KA2 impact on different levels Develop experience-based input to the new Erasmus+ programme The conference will focus especially on: the strategic and systemic impact of KA2 projects; quality, sustainability and long-term use of KA2 outcomes; the contribution of KA2 to youth work, youth participation and youth policy development as well as cross-sectoral cooperation and learning for youth; cooperation between organisations, sectors and countries; and the future role of KA2 within the next Erasmus+ programme. Participants as active contributors We invite participants to actively contribute to the programme and collective learning process. In the application form, participants will have the opportunity to propose ideas and contributions connected to their KA2 experience and expertise. You may wish to: facilitate a showcase workshop or practice-sharing session; present a KA2 outcome, method, tool or learning approach in the marketplace; host or co-host a roundtable discussion on a strategic challenge, dilemma or future perspective related to KA2; contribute to discussions on impact, sustainability, policy relevance or future programme development; or act as a “critical friend” bringing reflections and questions from your own national or thematic perspective. We especially encourage contributions that: demonstrate strategic or systemic impact; connect local realities with European priorities; share lessons learned, including challenges and failures; and inspire cooperation, sustainability and wider use of KA2 outcomes. During the event, all participants will engage with: reflections based on the mapping of KA2 projects implemented between 2021–2025; workshops and a marketplace of inspiring KA2 practices; peer-learning linked to KA2 quality criteria; discussions on impact, monitoring and sustainability; and collaborative work on recommendations for the future generation of KA2. The conference will also create strong opportunities for networking and partnership-building between experienced KA2 beneficiaries, National Agencies, European networks and policy-level stakeholders. Methods and methodology KA2NOW is designed as a participatory and practice-oriented conference combining strategic reflection, peer learning, policy dialogue and experiential exchange. The methodology includes: roundtables and peer-learning workshops; KA2 marketplace and best practice showcases; thematic discussions linked to Erasmus+ priorities and the European Youth Work Agenda; networking and partnership-building activities; evidence collection and reflection on KA2 impact and sustainability; collaborative recommendation-building for the future Erasmus+ programme; and elements of “action research”, including participant reflections, mapping analysis and knowledge harvesting during the event itself. The conference aims to create a balanced space where practitioners, National Agencies and policy-makers can jointly reflect on: what makes KA2 projects meaningful and strategic; how KA2 outcomes can create wider impact beyond individual organisations; and what future programme structures and support mechanisms are needed to strengthen the quality and relevance of cooperation partnerships in Europe. Who is the event for? KA2NOW will bring together approximately 100–150 participants from across Europe

19874.testo: Open call for youth workers (18+) from Albania, Georgia, Germany, Spain, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland and Slovakia to join the Erasmus+ Training Course "Behind the Wheel," from 17 to 25 August 2026 in Bernāti, Latvia. The course strengthens youth workers' understanding of youth wellbeing and gives them practical tools to support young people's emotional balance, self-awareness and personal growth. About the Project "Behind the Wheel" is based on the idea that youth workers are often "behind the wheel" of the learning process: the way they communicate, facilitate activities and manage their own emotions and energy has a direct impact on young people's experiences and wellbeing. The course combines embodiment, mindfulness, coaching approaches and reflective practices to improve both personal and professional skills, with methods you can later integrate into youth exchanges, youth centres, schools and community work. What You'll Focus On 🧠 Understanding youth wellbeing and the challenges young people face today, such as stress, pressure and emotional disconnection 🤝 Exploring the role of youth workers in creating safe, inclusive and supportive learning environments 🔍 Developing self-awareness and emotional understanding through reflection and practical activities 🧘 Learning and practising mindfulness exercises, embodiment methods and body-awareness techniques 💬 Using coaching approaches and reflective tools to improve communication and personal development 👥 Strengthening group facilitation skills and creating meaningful learning experiences for young people 🌱 Discovering practical wellbeing-oriented methods for daily youth work Every Erasmus+ training course earns you a YouthPass. Here's what it is and why it matters: https://youthworkshub.org/15122/ Our Goal To strengthen youth workers' capacity to support young people's wellbeing, emotional resilience and self-awareness through practical, wellbeing-oriented methods and conscious facilitation, while also improving youth workers' own self-awareness and emotional management. Who Can Participate 🧑‍🏫 Youth workers responsible for youth programmes 🤝 NGO staff and volunteers in administrative roles 🌟 Young people (18 to 30) who directly benefit from NGO initiatives 📚 Educators, trainers and facilitators who collaborate with youth workers 🌍 Partner organisations and community members who wish to foster civic engagement and social cohesion Participants should be at least 18 years old. Eligible Countries 🇦🇱 Albania, 🇬🇪 Georgia, 🇩🇪 Germany, 🇪🇸 Spain, 🇱🇻 Latvia, 🇱🇹 Lithuania, 🇵🇱 Poland, 🇸🇰 Slovakia What to Bring 🩳 A swimsuit (the venue is near a white-sand beach, though it can be cold) 🧥 A warm jumper for cooler nights 👕 Comfortable clothes for indoor and outdoor activities 💊 Any medication you need during the project 💻 At least 1 to 2 laptops per country, so you can use digital tools 🍲 Traditional food to present your country at the cultural evening 🪪 Your European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) 🧴 A towel, toiletries and a reusable water bottle Essential Things to Know 🏥 Insurance: organisers provide local health insurance for accidents during the project, but this does not cover travel issues. Each participant is responsible for their own travel insurance (missed flights, delays, lost luggage, etc.), and organisers will not reimburse new tickets if your plans change 📣 Sharing your experience: as part of Erasmus+, you'll share your experience during and after the project (a social media post, video/reel, blog or organisation post) covering what Erasmus+ is, what you experienced and learned, and why you'd recommend it. Accoglie persone d'età, istruzione, status sociale e background culturale diversi. La struttura in cui verrai inserito è un centro giovanile: un luogo speciale per i giovani, perché vi possono sviluppare competenze sociali, artistiche e professionali. Sarai coinvolto attivamente in tutte le attività sia dell'ente di coordinamento che della struttura d'accoglienza, occupandoti dei social media e realizzando iniziative di tua ideazione, eventi, workshops e campagne informative; conoscerai culture diverse partecipando a vari progetti per i giovani, attività di beneficenza con ragazzi e organizzazioni giovanili di tutta la Lettonia ed eventi. Il viaggio d'andata e ritorno dall'Italia alla Lettonia ti sarà completamente rimborsato, e un'assicurazione convenzionata con l'Unione Europea ti coprirà in caso di incidenti. Lo staff dell'ente di coordinamento sarà sempre a tua disposizione per aiutarti a superare qualsiasi difficoltà tu possa incontrare entrando in un contesto così diverso dal tuo quotidiano. Questo volontariato è un'esperienza che vale veramente la pena fare, con ritmi intensi, piena di cose da imparare, di relazioni di gruppo e di momenti indimenticabili, sul lavoro e nei fine settimana. Participant profile Sei il volontario che cerchiamo se ti piace lavorare in gruppo, comunicare con i giovani e se hai tanta creatività. Sarebbe bello se avessi qualche interesse verso la fotografia, la registrazione e il montaggio di video, verso la comunicazione sui social media o nell'organizzazione degli eventi. Se hai delle idee per la preparazione di workshops o per fare nuove attività con i giovani, questo è il posto ideale per te!!!! Si tratta di un'esperienza che unisce azione e creatività, dove la passione per l'arte, le lingue, i libri o lo sport regna sovrana. Non sono necessarie conoscenze specifiche, ma solo tanto entusiasmo e voglia di coinvolgersi e d'imparare a fare cose nuove. 20740.testo: If you have ever felt that something is missing between a great workshop and lasting change in young people's lives, this training might be exactly what you have been looking for. Embodied Habits is a 9-day residential Erasmus+ Training Course in the Latvian countryside, where youth workers explore breath, yoga, dance, and improvisation as a framework for habit formation and embodied learning, translating the science of behaviour change into concrete youth work tools. About the Training This 9-day residential training course brings together 31 youth workers from 8 European countries to explore practical methodologies of breath, yoga, dance, and improvisation as a framework for habit formation and embodied learning. The methodology draws on James Clear's Atomic Habits, one of the most practical frameworks for understanding how behaviour change really works, and translates it into concrete youth work tools, not as theory but as something you can use on Monday morning. You will learn how small, consistent actions compound into real change, and how to design learning experiences that support young people in making that happen in their own lives. The training combines breathing techniques, yogic knowledge, dance, and improvisation with facilitation practice, peer exchange, and hands-on workshop design. At its core is an experimental, embodied approach: you encounter the methodology through your own body and experience before translating it into tools for your work with young people, in whatever context that happens. The Methodology and Daily Rhythm The daily structure of the course is itself part of the methodology. Since you cannot effectively teach habit formation without practising it, the programme is built around consistent daily rhythms, shared meals, physical activity, reduced screen time, and quality rest. Going to sleep at a reasonable hour is part of the programme, as a shared commitment to exploring whether the depth of connection you are looking for might be found in well-rested mornings rather than late nights. This also means the training asks something personal from participants. You will be invited to take responsibility for your own mental and physical health, to notice your own patterns honestly, and to explore through experience what sustainable living and working feels like. Community-supported self-exploration, embodied practice, and personal accountability are as central to this week as any session on the programme. What You Will Take Home 🧭 A clear methodological framework you can start applying straight away 📋 Practical session templates and facilitation tools 🛠️ A pilot workshop designed for your own group 🌍 A supportive European network of youth workers developing their habits 📜 A Youthpass certificate recognising your learning Who Can Apply 🎂 Aged 18 and over, actively involved in youth work with at least one year of practical experience 🤝 Currently working with target groups facing motivational, emotional, or social challenges 🗣️ A sufficient level of English (the working language) 📍 Able to travel to Latvia for the full duration (27 October to 6 November, travel days included) 📣 Willing to design and implement at least one local follow-up workshop after the training Selection prioritises candidates who work with young people with fewer opportunities, are interested in methodological development, and show commitment to knowledge transfer within their organisation. This training brings together youth workers from 🇭🇷 Croatia, 🇬🇷 Greece, 🇮🇹 Italy, 🇱🇻 Latvia, 🇵🇱 Poland, 🇸🇰 Slovakia, 🇸🇮 Slovenia, and 🇪🇸 Spain. Accommodation 🌲 The venue is Laumas Recreation Park in the scenic Talsi Municipality of Latvia, 20 km from Talsi, with a spacious guesthouse, a 100 m² seminar hall, and comfortable accommodation, surrounded by forests and educational nature trails 🥗 Vegetarian and vegan food options are available What's Covered 💚 Accommodation, food, and travel (within defined per-country limits) are funded by the EU. La missione dell’organizzazione è quella di coltivare l’indipendenza e la creatività nei giovani attraverso la danza, il circo, l’acrobatica, la recitazione e la musica. Il gruppo di istruttori e allievi condivide un’atmosfera amichevole e accogliente. Il tuo tempo come volontario si dividerà tra assitenza degli istruttori durante le sessioni di allenamento di circo e acrobazia e attività d’ufficio, adattate ai tuoi interessi e alle tue preferenze. Tuttavia, una parte significativa del tuo tempo verrà soprattutto trascorsa in palestra e i compiti specifici varieranno a seconda della tua esperienza pregressa, delle tue competenze e dei tuoi interessi. Potrai anche contribuire ad attività creative quali la coreografia, la creazione di costumi, la gestione dei social media o la realizzazione di contenuti visivi. Accommodation, food and transport arrangements Ti verrà fornito un alloggio adeguato, vicino al luogo di svolgimento del volontariato: in genere si tratta d'un appartamento condiviso o d'un ostello, arredati con le attrezzature di base. La sistemazione può essere singola o condivisa a seconda della disponibilità, con cucina e bagno in comune. Riceverai un contributo di 5 euro al giorno per le spese personali e altri 200 euro al mese per il vitto. Il viaggio dall'Italia all'Estonia e ritorno sarà completamente rimborsato, così come i trasporti locali relativi alle attività saranno interamente sostenuti dall'organizzazione d'accoglienza. Training during the activity Parteciperai a 3 sessioni di formazione ufficiali: una prima della partenza dall'Italia, una seconda qualche settimana dopo il tuo arrivo in Estonia e una terza verso la fine del volontariato. Acquisirai esperienza pratica nella ginnastica acrobatica e nel circo e competenze didattiche e di coaching, migliorerai la tua capacità di gestione del tempo, amplierai creatività e spirito d'iniziativa: in sintesi, questo volontariato sarà fonte di grande crescita personale, e tutto questo mentre ti farai tanti nuovi amici, anche grazie alle attività complementari organizzate dal Centro. Participant profile Cerchiamo volontari coraggiosi, curiosi e desiderosi d'imparare e contribuire alla crescita dell'organizzazione d'accoglienza, sicuri nelle loro scelte e determinati a portare a termine i cómpiti assegnati con il supporto dei mentor. È importante possedere interesse per lo sport, l'esercizio fisico e il lavoro con i bambini, ed essere disponibili a provare i numeri in prima persona, anche quelli acrobatici, prima di insegnarli ai beneficiari. Una precedente esperienza in ginnastica, circo o danza verrà valutata positivamente. Il lavoro dell'organizzazione d'accoglienza è dinamico e in continua evoluzione, quindi flessibilità, apertura a nuove esperienze e spigliatezza sono caratteristiche fondamentali per partecipare a questo progetto. Poiché tutte le sessioni di formazione si svolgono in Estone, è fondamentale che il volontario s'impegni attivamente nell'apprendimento di questa lingua. Inoltre, si prega di notare che le attività del centro non seguono l'orario di lavoro tradizionale e la giornata lavorativa tipica va dalle 12:00 alle 20:00 o dalle 13:00 alle 21:00. Come volontario, sarai chiamato a organizzare e gestire un club di lingua e cultura italiana presso la scuola locale; svolgere attività con i giovani presso la casa dei giovani di Lihula, interagendo con i ragazzi del posto che frequentano il centro dopo la scuola; scrivere una rubrica sulla vita dell'ESC e dei volontari almeno due volte al mese per Lääneranna Noorteportaal; svolgere attività con i giovani e attività culturali presso il Lõpe klubi un giorno a settimana e contribuire all'organizzazione di attività per i giovani presso il Kõmsi noortetuba. La sistemazione può essere singola o condivisa a seconda della disponibilità, con cucina e bagno in comune. Riceverai un contributo di 5 euro al giorno per le spese personali e altri 200 euro al mese per il vitto. Il viaggio dall'Italia all'Estonia e ritorno sarà completamente rimborsato, mente per gli spostamenti a Lääneranna ti verrà fornita una bicicletta . Infine, avrai il supporto di un mentor locale. Pertanto, è necessario essere pronti a lavorare in squadra e ad assumere un ruolo di supporto nell'organizzazione di eventi e attività per e con i giovani. Questo potrebbe richiedere a volte pazienza e comprensione, così come è importante saper lavorare in autonomia quando necessario. Lavorerai, infatti, oltre che con i bambini, anche a stretto contatto con il personale, costituito da responsabile del centro, assistenti sociali e infermieri. In sintesi, questo volontariato sarà fonte di grande crescita professionale e personale. Participant profile Cerchiamo un volontario con la passione per il lavoro con bambini e ragazzi, dotato di pazienza e in grado di comprendere e accettare che spesso provengono da contesti familiari e sociali difficili. Il volontario ideale dovrebbe inoltre essere amichevole e di mentalità aperta, proattivo, giocoso, ottimista e responsabile. 21340.testo: ReVive was born out of a desire to create more accessible and inclusive creative spaces, where making art is not limited by talent, financial resources or traditional ideas of what art should be or talk about. It is an invitation to look at the objects and materials around us with a different perspective, reconnecting with the joy of crafting and transforming what already exists. ✨ About the Project ReVive is a 10 day Youth Experiential Learning Program that wishes to bring together young queer people and allies from diverse backgrounds in a shared creative space to explore upcycled art and artistic expression through a hands on approach. The team aims to create a space where creativity can be explored freely, without pressure or expectations, offering the opportunity to experiment with discarded materials and objects. Through this process, you are invited to explore how creative practices can shape our experiences, being a tool to express ourselves, connect with others and perhaps see the world from different perspectives. From the very beginning, the experience is shaped together, creating community agreements to build a safer and braver space for living and working, while encouraging active participation, accountability, mutual support and collective care. For the team, living together is a very important part of the experience. This means sharing responsibilities, taking care of common spaces and each of us, in our own way, contributing to the atmosphere we want to create. This can be through daily tasks such as cleaning, tidying up, decorating the space, preparing breakfast, collaborating on creative projects or simply spending time together. By living and working together, everyone shares in the experience of being part of a collectively created community. This approach involves learning by doing and peer to peer learning, meaning learning from each other. You are part of an intercultural environment and, as much as possible, an intersectional space, and you have the chance to work individually, in pairs, in small teams and in a big group. 22571.testo: Climate change is no longer a distant headline — it is already shaping the daily lives, health and future of the young people you work with. Climate-Conscious Youth Work (2nd edition) is an Erasmus+ Training Course taking place from 13 to 20 October 2026 in the Kaunas district of Lithuania, bringing together youth workers, leaders and educators who want to bring climate and sustainability into their everyday practice with young people. At Youth Works Hub we gather fully funded training for youth workers, and this one turns a heavy global topic into something you can actually facilitate back home. You do not need to be a climate expert — the course is built precisely for those with little or no prior experience in the field. Why This Training Matters Young people are among the populations most exposed to the accelerating climate crisis. European research and policy analysis show that climate change is already affecting young people's physical health, deepening social inequalities and adding emotional strain — including the growing phenomenon of eco-anxiety. The Council of Europe and the European Commission both stress that young people are experiencing, and will continue to bear, the brunt of worsening climate impacts, which makes climate action not only an environmental issue but a matter of intergenerational justice. At the same time, youth engagement is increasingly recognised as a decisive force in Europe's green transition. Through both formal pathways (schools, civic participation) and informal ones (community projects, youth work), young people bring creativity, fresh perspectives and a direct stake in long-term solutions. The Council of Europe's Recommendation on Young People and Climate Action goes further, insisting that young people be meaningfully included in climate decision-making, that young climate defenders be protected, and that the structural barriers keeping youth out of policy be removed. This course sits exactly at that intersection — equipping the youth workers who stand between those young people and real, local action. 🎓 New to this format and what it involves? Here's the essential guide: What Is a Training Course? → https://youthworkshub.org/trainingcourse What You Will Explore Over eight days, through non-formal learning, you will: 🌍 Explore current global trends around climate change and sustainability, and how they connect to young people and youth work; 🌱 Build a shared understanding of what sustainability actually means and why it matters in youth work; 🔎 Unpack the complexity and the multiple perspectives surrounding climate challenges; ⚖️ Examine climate justice and equity as central to any real solution; 📚 Study real-life case studies of community-led and youth-led climate and sustainability initiatives; 🧰 Practise concrete non-formal tools and youth work approaches that help young people build competencies for sustainable living and active citizenship; 🗣️ Design sustainable, local and participatory climate action initiatives that amplify young people's voices; 🤝 Experience a safe, inclusive space for intercultural dialogue, exchange and partnership building. The draft programme runs day by day through group building, global trends, sustainability and resource depletion, the complexity of the climate crisis, climate justice and youth, the power of community, a climate activism case study, climate education, climate-friendly youth work, and finally building a climate-conscious action you can carry into your own organisation. 🌱 Prefer another sustainability-focused training abroad? Take a look at the Bioconstruction and Sustainable Building Training Course in 🇵🇹 Portugal → https://youthworkshub.org/20693 Who Can Apply This training is for youth workers, youth leaders and educators active in youth centres, youth organisations or any entity working with young people, as well as mentors, trainers and coordinators involved in local and/or international youth activities outside formal education. To take part, you should: 🌱 Have little or no prior experience in climate and sustainability topics — and the motivation to build that into your daily work; 🌍 Be a citizen or resident of an Erasmus+ Programme country (EU27 plus Türkiye, North Macedonia, Serbia, Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein); 🏢 Be connected to an organisation with an Erasmus+ OID number that agrees to act as your sending organisation; 📅 Not be taking part in another Erasmus+ long-term project (student exchange, European Solidarity Corps, Erasmus internship) during the training period; 🗣️ Have a good command of English and be able to join the entire programme. To keep the group balanced, the organisers will select no more than 3–4 participants per country. Costs and the Green Travel Bonus Accommodation and meals are fully provided and paid by the organisers. Participants stay at the Sadauskų sodyba homestead, surrounded by Lithuanian nature just outside Kaunas, in shared rooms of 3–4, with food cooked on site. Travel costs are reimbursed according to the European Commission's distance calculator (destination: Antalkiai). The organisers strongly encourage green travel — using low-emission transport such as train, bus or carpooling for the main part of your journey. Travel green and they can also reimburse accommodation (up to €70) and food (up to €60) for your extra travel days, up to €130 total. Reimbursement typically takes 4–6 weeks. Fittingly for a course on sustainability, the low-carbon route is not just rewarded on paper — it is part of the point. 🌱 Planning to travel green and get more for it? LEC (Love Every Challenge) is a 5-day leadership and self-development training for youth workers, trainers, volunteers, and educators who want to deepen self-awareness, strengthen resilience, and bring new methods back into their youth work. Working with young people can be rewarding — but also exhausting. Many youth workers feel stuck, overwhelmed, or unsure about their next steps. LEC offers a space to pause, reflect, and recharge while also learning tools that can be applied directly in their personal life and non-formal education settings. At the heart of LEC is the invitation to: “Become a leader you wish to follow.” This means learning to lead from your values, cultivating emotional intelligence, and embodying the resilience and courage that you wish to inspire in others. The training is based on the Swedish Value Based Leadership programme, enriched with synergy methods and our own 20 years of experience in experiential learning. We combine: - Adventure & outdoors: stretching comfort zones, building trust, and exploring leadership through symbolic challenges in nature. - Embodiment & community: movement, storytelling, role play, and sharing circles to explore emotions, values, and inner compass. - Experience & reflection: learning by doing, then transferring insights into daily life and youth work practice. Participants will: - Develop personal resilience and self-leadership, essential in preventing burnout. - Gain practical tools for group facilitation, reflection processes, and working with challenges. - Strengthen their emotional intelligence and ability to support young people in transitions and difficulties. - Join a community of youth workers from Latvia and other European countries, sharing experiences and building networks for future cooperation. For the 20th time, Piedzīvojuma Gars invites you to this training in the Latvian countryside — far from distractions, close to nature, and surrounded by peers. More than 300 participants have already joined, many describing it as a turning point in both life and work. When: 18 - 22 October 2026 Where: Rites countryside home, Latvia Who: Youth workers, trainers, volunteers, educators, and others active in the youth field (18+) PLEASE READ FULL DESCRIPTION here before applying: https://www.piedzivojumagars.lv/lec.html

30366.testo: A 7-day Erasmus+ training exploring dreamwork, embodiment, expressive arts and nature-based practices, offering experiential methods and tools for youth workers to bring into their work with young people and communities. It is dark, our eyes drop heavy, and behind them another world invites us in, no matter if we remember that world upon waking. As our bodies rest, our psyche takes us towards images, memories, emotions and stories that often remain outside our everyday awareness. Dreaming from the Mycelium of the Earth is an invitation. An invitation to become curious about the intelligence that lives beneath our usual ways of knowing. Like mycelium moving quietly beneath the forest floor, much of what shapes us remains unseen. An invitation to tend dreams as wild and meaningful parts of ourselves. An invitation to be guided by dreams, movement, art, imagination and nature — allowing them to move with us and within us. And an invitation to explore how these practices can enrich youth work and non-formal education, creating spaces where young people can deepen their relationship with themselves, their communities and the more-than-human world. Dreaming from the Mycelium of the Earth is a 7-day Erasmus+ training course combining dreamwork, embodiment, storytelling, poetry, expressive arts, deep imagination and ecological and nature-based education. The training will offer youth workers and other professionals working with people a space to first experience these approaches themselves and then explore how they can be adapted to their own educational contexts. We believe that meaningful youth work begins not only with methods, but also with the capacity of the practitioner to be present, listen, notice, imagine and create spaces where different ways of knowing and expressing ourselves are welcomed. Throughout the programme, participants will therefore move between personal experience, group learning and professional reflection: What does this practice awaken in me? What does it teach me as a facilitator? How could it support the young people and communities I work with? The deep winter landscape of rural Latvia will become part of our learning environment — a place for slowing down, listening, creating, moving and experimenting. We hope participants will leave with new resources, perspectives and practical methods that can be brought back into their youth work, educational activities and communities. DURING THE TRAINING WE WILL EXPLORE - dream-tending and approaches to working with dreams; - embodiment and somatic awareness; - movement and expressive arts; - storytelling and poetry; - deep imagination; - nature-based and experiential learning; - ecological awareness and relationship with the more-than-human world; - reflection and council practices; - intercultural learning; - resilience and self-care; - ways of adapting experiential and creative practices to youth work and non-formal education. The methodology will be highly experiential. Participants should be willing to engage actively in individual practices, group processes, creative exploration, time outdoors and reflection. YOUTH WORK & LEARNING An important part of the training will be exploring how creative, embodied and nature-based approaches can support contemporary youth work. Young people increasingly need spaces where they can slow down, reconnect with their bodies and creativity, explore identity and emotions, experience meaningful relationships and develop a deeper sense of belonging to their communities and the natural world. The training aims to expand the methodological toolbox of youth workers by introducing practices that can support self-expression, self-awareness, creativity, emotional resilience, connection, participation and ecological awareness. Participants will be invited to reflect on how the methods experienced during the programme can be adapted responsibly to different groups of young people and different educational and community contexts. The intention is therefore not to train participants to become therapists or dream analysts. Instead, we will explore dream, imagination, embodiment, art and nature as creative and educational resources within non-formal learning and youth work. WHO IS IT FOR? We are calling in people who work with people — those who create spaces for learning, growth, connection and transformation. The programme is particularly relevant for: youth workers, facilitators, educators, mentors, coaches, guides, artists, community workers and nature-based practitioners, as well as those whose work does not quite fit into a single box. You do not need to arrive as an expert, nor do you need previous experience with dreamwork or nature-based practices. We are more interested in your curiosity: your willingness to listen, experiment, participate fully and bring what you discover back into the communities and people you work with. Participants must: be 18 years or older; be able to communicate and participate in English; be willing to participate in the whole programme; be interested in applying or sharing the learning in their youth work, educational practice or communities; legally reside in one of the participating countries. Applications are open to residents of: Latvia, Romania, Cyprus, Italy, Iceland, Estonia, Czechia and Slovakia. DATES & LOCATION 4–12 December 2026 4 December — arrival day and organised transportation from Riga to the venue 5–11 December — 7 full programme days 12 December — departure and organised transportation back to Riga The training will take place at Vonadziņi, Stāmeriena, in a rural area of North-Eastern Latvia.

The project was created in response to the growing need for youth workers to strengthen their emotional resilience, prevent burnout and develop practical tools for maintaining balance in both their personal and professional lives. During the training, participants will explore a wide range of creative, mindfulness, body-based, artistic and experiential practices that can be adapted to everyday youth work. Objectives and Topics The project explores creative and experiential approaches to emotional well-being, self-reflection and professional sustainability in youth work. The main objectives are to expand emotional well-being tools by exploring mindfulness, meditation, creative practices, performative arts and improvisational theatre; strengthen self-reflection and emotional resilience by developing awareness of emotions, personal boundaries, inner balance and burnout prevention; encourage creativity as a tool for self-expression, emotional self-regulation and personal development; introduce innovative methods that can be adapted and integrated into everyday youth work practice; support sustainable transfer by helping participants bring new methods into their organisations, activities and work with young people; and create opportunities for international cooperation through sharing experiences, methods and good practices with youth workers from different countries. Participant Profile Participants must be youth workers, educators, youth organisation representatives, active volunteers or other professionals actively working with young people. They should be interested in emotional well-being, self-reflection and creative approaches to personal and professional development, and be open to exploring alternative and experiential methods, including art, movement, performance, improvisation and mindfulness. Participants should also be ready to share experiences and good practices with youth workers from other European countries. Expected Results and Impact By participating in the project, youth workers will gain new practical tools for emotional well-being, including mindfulness, creative practices, performative arts and improvisational theatre. They will strengthen self-reflection, emotional resilience and self-regulation while developing greater awareness of personal boundaries and burnout prevention. Participants will discover creative and experiential methods that can be used in everyday youth work, including creative writing, playback theatre, nonviolent communication (NVC), movement and body-awareness practices. They will develop greater confidence and creativity when responding to emotional and professional challenges in youth work, learn how to adapt and transfer new methods to different groups of young people and integrate them into their organisations, and contribute to a more innovative and sustainable youth work sector where emotional well-being, creativity and experiential learning become part of everyday practice. 30821.testo: The Clown In You is an Erasmus+ training course in Estonia, from 20 to 27 January 2027, where youth workers and educators dive into clowning, improv and personal exploration techniques. The training aims to enrich the toolbox of a youth worker and to give participants the chance to learn about themselves and explore personal boundaries, acquiring clowning techniques along the way. Applications close on 15 October 2026. At Youth Works Hub, we reviewed the infopack, the application form and the organiser's policies so you know exactly what you are signing up for. Shokkin Group Estonia hosts the course at Vanaõue Puhkekeskus in Vihi, with a final stop in Tallinn. No prior experience with clowning or theatre is required: participants only need to be willing to explore new techniques and able to join the full training timeline. The application form asks you to confirm that you are aware of a 30 EUR advised contribution for the training course. What the Training Is About In a hands-on manner, a group of international participants, supported by the hosting and training team, dives into clowning, improv and personal exploration techniques. The training aims to enrich the toolbox of a youth worker and to give the possibility to learn about oneself and explore personal boundaries. The programme works with two art forms, clowning and bouffon, and it prepares participants to use the techniques in direct work with young people, for example in communication trainings for young people. What You Will Gain The infopack lists four expected outcomes: 🎭 A clear understanding of clowning and bouffon art forms. 🧭 An exploration of personal boundaries with the art of clowning. 🧰 A set of methods and practice techniques to use in direct work with young people (for example using techniques in communication trainings for young people). 😎 A confident attitude and the chance to find your clown personality. The Training Timeline 📅 Preparation online meeting: 12 January 2027 at 18:00 CET, 60 minutes. 📍 In-person training activity: 20 to 27 January 2027. 📣 Local dissemination activities: January to April. 🖥️ Final online meeting: early April, 60 minutes. An Intense Daily Rhythm According to the organiser's Event Policy 2026, the event has an intense schedule. Most days include three practical sessions of 90 minutes and a last session of 60 minutes, with designated time for reflection. To guarantee your full involvement, selected participants are expected not to plan any online meetings or appointments during the training programme hours, 9:50 to 19:00 EET. Any work or study related meetings must be done during break or free time slots. Participants are also expected to use mobile devices and equipment during session times only for emergencies or for assistance with the activity itself. The preliminary schedule is linked in the Links section. What to Bring and How to Dress Because the training is an immersive experience of exploring clowning and creating your own clown character, the training team asks participants to review the safer space policy and to commit to the following: 🖤 Clothing: during the training sessions, wear comfortable plain black clothing without any writing, logos or slogans. 🎁 A personal object: bring one object. Do not overthink the choice: choose it impulsively, and it should be something you like. It can be silly or seemingly meaningless. 🎩 Clown costume items: on the final day you design a clown costume and create a complete character. Bring a few pieces of clothing (trousers, skirts, shoes) and accessories (hat, wig, tie) from home or your family that are very loose, very tight, very small, very large, very long or very short. Participants wear these items and exchange them during the games. 🚰 A water bottle: bring your personal water bottle to use inside the training room. 🧦 Indoor footwear: inside the venue, wear socks, slippers or indoor shoes. 🧺 Towels: provided by the venue. Who Can Apply The training is for people in the youth work and education sector: 🎂 Age: 18 or older, with no upper age limit. 👥 Profile: youth workers, non-formal educators, trainers, camp leaders, teachers, VET and higher education teaching staff, and student union representatives. Our guide to the role of youth workers explains how these roles fit into Erasmus+ projects. 🎭 Previous experience: no prior experience with clowning or theatre is required. Candidates should be willing to explore new techniques and able to join the full training timeline. 🗣️ Working language: participants are expected to be able to follow the training and cooperate in groups using English. The form asks you to rate your English level. 🌍 Countries: the training is open to official residents of the 33 countries listed in the Project Snapshot, which are the EU member states plus six further countries. Commitments You Make 📣 Dissemination: participants commit to local dissemination activities. This means organising at least one clowning or improv workshop with educators or young people per partner country within 2 months after the activity, and writing and publishing an article that summarises the training course experience on the sending organisation's online channel or another appropriate one. 🏥 Insurance: a valid medical insurance, for example the European Health Insurance Card (EHIC), is mandatory during your travel, together with a separate travel insurance that must cover damage or loss of luggage, accidents and serious illness, and death. Each participant covers the costs and provides proof of medical and travel insurance upon the coordinators' request. 🏷️ Advised contribution: the form asks you to confirm that you are aware of the 30 EUR advised contribution for the training course. The infopack and the policies do not say what it covers or when it is paid. 📸 Photos and videos: pictures and videos taken during the activities might be used to document the training and to promote the project in reports, partner websites, social media acc

30866.testo: "Embodied Belonging" is an Erasmus+ training in Latvia exploring eco-somatics, movement, and nature connection. For youth workers to cultivate presence, nervous system regulation, and grounded belonging to support youth well-being. Activity Description Embodied Belonging is an experiential Erasmus+ training course held in the quiet winter landscape of Latvia, designed to offer youth workers, trainers, and educators transformative tools rooted in eco-somatics, movement, and nature connection. When the outer world freezes into white silence, this course invites us to turn inward—exploring how belonging can be felt as a grounded, inner state of being within our own skin. By integrating body awareness, nervous system regulation, and outdoor immersion into non-formal education, participants will learn how to support both themselves and young people in feeling more connected, present, and resilient. Target Audience & Non-Formal Learning Context This training is specifically tailored for 28 participants working in non-formal learning and youth work (youth workers, trainers, facilitators, space holders, and educators aged 22+) who interact directly with young people, including those working with marginalized or disadvantaged youth. The program bridges personal practice and professional youth work methodology. Participants will gain practical, experiential NFE methods to bring fresh creativity, somatic grounding, and nature-based tools back to their local youth work practices. Main Themes & Methodology Eco-Somatics & Nervous System Regulation: Body-based tools to support youth mental health, emotional grounding, and self-care. Relational Awareness & Communication: Nonviolent Communication (NVC), consent practices, Playfight, and empathetic sharing circles. Movement & Creative Expression: Contact-inspired movement, dance jams, and sensory exercises. Nature Immersions: Silent walks, winter hiking, and forest bathing in snow-covered pine forests. Project Phases & Commitment Selected participants commit to all three project phases: Preparation: Pre-departure orientation and self-assessment. 10-Day Training Mobility: Full participation in Latvia (January 18–29, 2027). Follow-Up: Facilitating at least one local non-formal workshop within two months of returning home to share these tools with young people in their communities. Logistics & Practicalities Venue: Laumas Guest House, Talsi Municipality, Latvia (a secluded forest sanctuary). Atmosphere: An alcohol and drug-free learning environment. Funding: Food, accommodation, and program costs are fully covered by Erasmus+. Travel reimbursement is provided up to Erasmus+ distance band limits. Eligible Countries: Spain, France, Slovenia, Italy, and Latvia. Apply here: https://forms.gle/WPQCs2pHuRRom5BK9

A webinar on resources for youth workers and educators to work on the topics of life and career choices, mental health and critical thinking with young people. Thursday, 12th of November, 13:00 - 14:00 CET The project in a nutshell: Our goal is simple: help young people feel more ready for life - and give youth workers and educators better tools to support them. “Ready 4 Life: MindShift” is an Erasmus+ Youth partnership project that strengthens young people’s capacity to navigate information overload, mental well-being challenges, and complex life and career decisions. The project combines research, youth-friendly digital content, and practical tools for youth workers and educators. The focus topics of the project are: (a) life and career choices, (b) mental health, and (c) critical thinking and media literacy. The target groups of the project are: (1) young people in transition to adulthood, and (2) youth workers and educators. The context: The transition to adulthood has become increasingly complex due to digital information overload, rising mental health struggles, and overwhelming career choices. Young people often lack the skills, guidance, and accessible resources necessary to navigate these challenges effectively. Educators and youth workers, particularly in rural areas, also face difficulties in finding engaging, structured tools to support youth in these critical areas. 31254.testo: Y.E.S. is an international training course on developing inclusive youth projects, designing Erasmus+ funding applications and planning projects for diverse youth groups. The training will be in Russian. The training aims to develop participants’ practical skills in designing inclusive youth projects for diverse youth groups, preparing Erasmus+ funding applications and planning the successful implementation of their own projects. During the course, participants will explore the opportunities offered by the Erasmus+ programme, focusing on youth exchanges and training courses. They will learn how to choose the most appropriate project format for their ideas and how to develop a project from the initial analysis of the target group’s needs to the definition of objectives, methods and expected outcomes. The course will introduce participants to the logic of project development and the key elements of a funding application, ensuring a clear connection between identified needs, project objectives, planned activities, budget and evaluation. A particular focus will be placed on social inclusion and working with diverse youth groups. Participants will explore how to identify barriers to participation, take different needs into account at every stage of a project, and create accessible activities for young people with different abilities, backgrounds and levels of experience. They will learn how to adapt non-formal education methods, organise activities inclusively and provide appropriate support to participants. Participants will also develop their own project ideas, work on the key sections of an Erasmus+ funding application and identify the next steps towards preparing and implementing their projects. The training provides an opportunity to strengthen practical project development skills, exchange experiences with youth workers from different countries and explore opportunities for international cooperation within the Erasmus+ programme. The training is designed as a practical learning process that connects the principles of inclusion with the concrete stages of project development, from identifying needs and designing activities to preparing funding applications and planning implementation. Objectives of the training The main objective of the training is to develop participants’ competencies in designing inclusive youth projects, preparing Erasmus+ funding applications and planning activities that respond to the needs of diverse youth groups. By the end of the training, participants will: explore the opportunities offered by the Erasmus+ programme, including youth exchanges and training courses; learn how to choose the appropriate Erasmus+ project format for their ideas; understand the principles of social inclusion and identify barriers that may prevent young people from participating in projects; learn how to analyse the needs of a target group and translate them into clear project objectives; develop skills in selecting appropriate non-formal education methods and defining expected project outcomes; understand the structure of an Erasmus+ funding application and the connections between needs, objectives, activities, budget and evaluation; learn how to plan accessible activities for diverse youth groups with different abilities and levels of experience; explore how to adapt methods, organisational arrangements and participant support to different needs; develop their own project ideas and prepare key sections of an Erasmus+ funding application; identify the next steps towards preparing and implementing their projects; become more confident in applying the knowledge and methods gained during the training to their future youth work. Target group – the training is aimed at: youth workers; leaders of youth non-governmental organisations; educators and trainers; people interested in developing their own projects within the Erasmus+ programme; people who have experience or motivation to work with youth groups and are interested in inclusive youth work and international cooperation. Participants are expected to have experience or a willingness to work with youth groups, be ready to use non-formal education methods and actively participate in all course activities. They should be motivated to develop their professional skills in youth work and be willing to apply the knowledge gained during the training in their future activities and projects. Methodology The training focuses on practical learning, active participation and the application of non-formal education methods. Participants will explore the Erasmus+ programme, analyse the needs of different youth groups, examine the principles of social inclusion and work through the key stages of project development. The learning process will combine individual work, group activities, discussions, experience sharing and practical project development tasks. Participants will work on their own project ideas, define objectives and expected outcomes, select appropriate methods and develop key sections of a funding application. Particular attention will be given to ensuring that project activities are accessible and that the needs of diverse participants are considered throughout the project cycle. The methodology connects theoretical understanding with practical application, enabling participants to leave the training with a clearer understanding of the Erasmus+ programme and concrete foundations for developing their own inclusive youth projects.

31255.testo: Youth work in rural areas faces unique challenges and opportunities. Gillian Cowell from the British Council, the UK National Agency, will share this exciting news. The current Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps programme period is ending in 2027, and preparations for the new programme period (2028–2034) are already underway. Andreas Bosshard from SALTO Inclusion & Diversity will provide an update on the future programme period and its inclusion and diversity priorities. Examples of how the programmes are being used in rural areas. Organisations from across Europe will share how Erasmus+ and ESC projects have transformed their work with young people. This seminar follows the residential training course "Youth Work in Rural Areas – European Seminar", held in May 2026 in Manosque, France. Silvia Di Passio from the Italian National Agency will summarise the key takeaways from the event. Who should join This seminar is for representatives of organizations working in rural areas, who: Work with young people or plan to start working with youngsters; Have the interest, capacity and support to implement Erasmus+: Youth in Action and European Solidarity Corps projects Are able to work in English. Testimonials of the organizations using Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps programmes for rural youth 15:40 BREAK (15 min) 15.55 Looking Ahead: where are the programmes heading, and what does this mean for rural youth work? 16:45 The end of the seminar All times are in Central Europe Time, please convert them to your local time zone! Please note that the organisers reserve the right to make changes to the programme if necessary. The Strategic Partnership on Inclusion (SPI) This activity is part of the Strategic Partnership on Inclusion (SPI). The Strategic Partnership for Inclusion is a Strategic National Agency Cooperation. Are you interested in applying for Erasmus+ KA2 Small-Scale Partnership Project in 2027 focused on youth participation? Then the Online Challenge is for you! Apply by 26 November 2026, together with your team and your partner(s)! This edition of the Online Challenge aims to support those interested in submitting their E+ KA2 projects by the March 2027 deadline through tailored learning and mentorship opportunities. During the Online Challenge, you can: develop the idea and write a real KA2 small-scale partnership project focused on youth participation bring your partner (already identified) or find relevant international partner(s) for the project and develop the project application together with them learn about youth participation and how it translates into competence building and strategic approaches for your organisation/community learn about quality elements of an Erasmus+ project get tailored and quality support from mentors (experienced in developing/assessing E+ KA2) who will help you to transfer your project idea into the application form take part in e-learning modules and weekly tasks connected to youth participation and project writing get a YouthPass (if you are part of at least 80% of all activities in the challenge). February-March 2027 you can get into this phase only if you have a relevant project idea, fitting in KA2 small-scale partnership projects, with a clear focus on youth participation; work with a mentor to develop your project idea (each mentor has allocated up to 8 hours/project to offer tailored feedback); complete weekly assignments designed to help you write the project application. Examples of types of partnerships supported through the Online Challenge and KA2 small-scale partnerships: Youth work associations aiming at building the capacity of their staff on supporting meaningful youth participation and exploring alternative forms of participation Youth-led NGOs upskilling their long-term activists in order to reach more young people with fewer opportunities, giving a voice to underrepresented youth Municipalities learning from each other on how to set up effective youth participation mechanisms in decision-making processes at local level Civil society organisations cooperating with youth centres and schools in order to improve civic education and youth participation cross-sectorally Umbrella organisations in the youth field developing common materials / games / resources that would mainstream youth participation at any level Advocacy organisations for certain groups of young people with fewer opportunities working together to gain competencies in advocacy and preparing recommendations for strategic influence on youth policy What is a KA2 small-scale partnership? a transnational project with a minimum of 2 organisations from 2 different Programme Countries lasts between 6 and 24 months, with a fixed lump sum of either €30,000 or €60,000 a simplified application form, designed as an entry point for newcomers and small organisations submitted by one partner to its own National Agency, by the March 2027 deadline responds to the following main objectives increasing quality in the work and practices of the organisations and institutions involved, building capacity of organisations to work transnationally and across sectors; addressing common needs and priorities mainly in the field of youth; enabling transformation and change (at individual, organisational or sectoral level) The main platform for online sessions will be ZOOM (Central European Time); additional online platforms will be used to facilitate the learning. Access to a personal computer and the Internet is required for all online meetings and activities. The Online Challenge is part of the strategic partnership New Power in Youth (NPiY SNAC), between several Erasmus+ National Agencies in the field of youth and SALTO Resource Centres. Other NAs are welcome to support participants in this activity, even if they are not part of the NPiY SNAC. Discover more about New Power in Youth via LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/new-power-in-youth/ Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/newpowerinyouth

31327.testo: A practical, participatory training for youth workers exploring LEGO® Serious Play®, Design Thinking, graphic facilitation and intercultural learning to expand their facilitation toolbox and discover creative ways of working with groups. During the training course, you will have the opportunity to learn by doing, exchange experiences with other youth workers, experiment with creative facilitation tools, and work together to develop methods that respond to real needs in youth work. You will leave the training with new skills, practical tools, draft facilitation methods, and an action plan for testing your learning in your local context. Most importantly, you will become part of a collaborative learning process that connects individual development with the wider goal of creating more inclusive, creative, and participatory learning opportunities for young people. The aim of the training course is to equip youth workers and educators from partner countries with practical skills, creative tools, and inclusive facilitation approaches that they can use to design and deliver engaging, participatory, and intercultural learning experiences in their local communities. Key Objectives: to strengthen facilitation skills by understanding the principles of facilitation and intercultural communication; to explore and apply LEGO® Serious Play® as a creative, hands-on approach to encourage participation, support reflection, explore different perspectives, and facilitate group discussions and problem-solving; to develop basic graphic facilitation skills by using basic visual elements and techniques; to learn the basics of the Design Thinking; to apply Design Thinking principles to identify needs, frame challenges, generate ideas, evaluate solutions, and design structured workshops and learning activities; to promote inclusion and intercultural learning by exploring facilitation approaches that value diversity, encourage equal participation, respect different perspectives, and support meaningful dialogue; to co-create new creative facilitation methods in small international teams, connecting the acquired tools and approaches to the thematic areas of Culture, Intercultural Learning, Social Inclusion, Human Rights, Training, Diversity, Non-formal Learning, and Design Thinking; to strengthen international cooperation and peer learning by sharing experiences, exchanging good practices, and learning from the different professional and cultural backgrounds of fellow participants. Participants' profile: The training is designed for youth workers, educators, trainers, and facilitators who are interested in improving the quality of their work with young people through creative, inclusive, and participatory learning methods. We welcome both volunteers and professionals working in local organisations, NGOs, educational institutions, youth centres, or other initiatives that support young people at local, regional, national, or international levels. Selection criteria: 18+ years old; have a communicative level of English; are actively involved in youth work or education, either as volunteers or professionals, and have opportunities to apply the learning in their work with young people; are motivated to develop their facilitation skills and explore creative methods such as LEGO® Serious Play®, graphic facilitation, and Design Thinking; have experience working with young people from diverse backgrounds, particularly in intercultural settings or with young people with fewer opportunities, including minorities and groups at risk of social exclusion; are willing to share their experiences and learn from others in an international environment, contributing to peer learning and intercultural exchange; are ready to engage actively in non-formal learning, including practical exercises, teamwork, experimentation, self-reflection, and collaborative method development; are willing to contribute to the project's follow-up activities by testing or adapting the newly developed methods and organising or supporting pilot workshops in their local, national, or international contexts; can commit to the full duration of the 8-day training and actively participate in the programme and its learning activities. Selected participants are in charge of organising a local event (seminar, workshop etc) for own community within 2 months after the training course comes to an end. Selected participants are in charge of dissemination and visibility activities of the project. More info: https://canva.link/f4a9kpzgyqii1p4

31420.testo: Youth Exchange bringing 32 young people from Lithuania, Türkiye, Italy and Spain together to explore career paths, develop skills, build motivation and create career plans. Erasmus+ Youth Exchange taking place in Kaunas, Lithuania, from 18–27 November 2026. The project brings together 32 young people from Lithuania, Türkiye, Italy and Spain for an international learning experience focused on career development and personal growth. Many young people at the beginning of their careers struggle to identify a professional path that matches their interests, strengths and goals. They may lack knowledge about available opportunities, awareness of their competencies, or a clear plan for developing their skills. This can lead to uncertainty about their future, whether they are studying, working or not yet engaged in career activities. During the eight-day exchange, participants will explore different professional opportunities and career paths, assess their competencies and identify areas for improvement. Through interactive and inclusive non-formal learning activities, they will work on developing a positive mindset, discovering their career motivation and creating short- and long-term personal development plans. The project also focuses on the role of non-formal learning, mentorship and international experience in professional development. By bringing together young people from different countries, the exchange creates an opportunity to share experiences, approaches and perspectives on career choices while challenging stereotypes connected to professional paths. The project aims to have an impact beyond the mobility itself. Following the exchange, participants will establish Career Advancement Clubs in their home countries. These clubs will provide local spaces where young people can meet, exchange experiences, explore career opportunities, develop practical skills and support one another in achieving their professional goals. Through these follow-up activities, participants will transfer the knowledge and tools gained during the exchange to their local communities and adapt them to the needs of young people in their respective contexts.

31900.testo:
Join a 2-9 month volunteering experience in rural Latvia. Support preschool children (ages 1.5–6) as they grow, play, and explore nature. Be part of daily preschool life and outdoor forest activities. Our project focuses on three big themes: green thinking & sustainability, social inclusion & community growth, and creative use of digital tools. You'll also have the chance to run workshops for locals — teenagers and adults alike - from arts and sports to languages, robotics, or digital skills. Opportunity to work in the local Youth centre and High school. We offer a safe, inspiring space with passionate educators, nature all around, and freedom to shape your own experience. We have a really cool boxing and well as regular gym just around the corner, a possibility to sing in a latvian choir, lakes and nature paths all around the city and bus/train lines connected to our capital Riga so you can explore city life on the weekends!

Volunteers receive on-arrival training from NA and ongoing support from preschool and school teachers and the community around us. Additionally, there are meetings with the project coordinator to set learning goals and aims for learning in all aspects (personal, professional, interpersonal). Some volunteers after the project have become excellent preschool teachers who went to study this field at the university, some took totally different paths, but all have learned and developed.
We are looking for an open and outgoing person, eager to learn and communicate. Likes the great outdoors. A person who wants to experience some type of mild Nordic weather living, meet spring with open arms and experience a summer of the unknown. If you feel ready for action and learning with some active and creative kids, then this is for you. We have tonns of references, we can connect you with our previous volunteer network and make sure you feel welcomed and a big part of our international community.
